shots.prompt: Night. Symmetrical frontal wide of a hillside observatory: the dome slit stands open and a blade of warm gold light escapes it; one bright red point - Mars - sits dead center above the dome. No people. The slit rumbles wider as the camera pushes slowly toward it until the glow fills the frame.

shots.prompt: Macro across a brass-and-bakelite observatory console: trembling dials, punched tape, glowing valves, and a round oscilloscope tube drawing a warm gold waveform, centered. No people. The waveform pulses like a voice; slow lateral drift ending centered on the scope screen.
shots.still: Macro across a brass-and-bakelite observatory console: trembling dials, punched tape, glowing valves, and a round oscilloscope tube drawing a warm gold waveform, centered. No people.

shots.lyric: Hey, I need you for something. / It's important.
shots.prompt: Medium frontal shot, perfectly centered: {{astronomer}} at a desk laid with specimen trays, translucent organic fragments and spectrogram strips, a brass telescope behind her, warm tungsten pools in darkness. She faces the lens, mouth open mid-phrase, deadpan self-assurance. She sings straight to camera with confident, punchy delivery - words clearly articulated, eyes locked on the lens, head steady, a subtle groove in her shoulders on the beat. Locked off.
shots.still: Medium frontal shot, perfectly centered: {{astronomer}} at a desk laid with specimen trays, translucent organic fragments and spectrogram strips, a brass telescope behind her, warm tungsten pools in darkness. She faces the lens, mouth open mid-phrase, deadpan self-assurance.

shots.prompt: Top-down overhead macro on a leather desktop: fragments of an alien specimen laid out like a puzzle - translucent organic shards with a helical, DNA-like structure visible inside, edges that almost interlock - beside a brass loupe and a spectrogram strip; tweed-cuffed hands hold two fragments whose helices almost line up. Only the hands are in frame; no people. The hands slide the fragments together; the helices almost meet, then miss by a hair, again and again. Slow overhead push-in.
